items.reason: ADR-0011 already named this gap in its own Consequences — 'the list can lie about GitHub's settings, because nothing here can read them without a token' — so the fix was to close that residue rather than restate the enumeration. The GitHub side is now written down as .github/branch-ruleset.json, a literal Rulesets payload whose required_status_checks contexts are exactly the five `check` strings in .github/required-checks.json (the rubric review among them), with the admin bypass the push-to-deploy model requires and the `gh api` line that applies it. scripts/branch-protection.mjs holds both halves: offline and blocking via checkDeclaredRuleset(), called from scripts/merge-gate.mjs inside `npm run check:ci` and therefore inside .husky/pre-push, so adding a required check and forgetting the ruleset — or an `evaluate` enforcement, or drifted wording — is a red build; and `--verify`, which reads GET /rules/branches/{branch} with the repo's own read token and reports check by check what GitHub is ACTUALLY enforcing. The weekly agent-review-history.yml runs that verification and appends the answer to review-history.md, which the publish job rewrites into the trail issue, so 'does the rubric review block a merge or only comment?' has a linkable answer readable by anyone with read access instead of only from inside a settings page. Three new tests in test-unit/delivery-contract.test.mjs fail if the ruleset stops matching the enumeration, if merge-gate stops checking it, or if the weekly verification or its append is removed. Stated honestly in the report itself and in the ADR: that API returns rulesets only, so a 'no' means no ruleset requires the check, never that the branch is unprotected — the classic endpoint needs an admin token GITHUB_TOKEN cannot be granted. Whether the operator has applied the declared ruleset is now reported rather than assumed, which is the observability the item asked for.

eslint.config.mjs now carries three repository-specific fences on top of the vendor config, each encoding a constraint AGENTS.md previously stated only in prose, and each verified against the tree before landing so it is blocking rather than reporting (ADR-0007): (1) the LLM chokepoint — `GoogleGenAI` may not be constructed outside src/lib/llm/, and the three provider adapters (@/lib/llm/gemini|claude|codex) may only be reached for their availability probe, which is the single existing exception (src/app/api/ai/status/route.ts); (2) the store seam — `firebase-admin`, `firebase-admin/*` and `node:sqlite` are refused outside src/lib/, so a route or component cannot pick a backend, break LOCAL_DB, or skip the tenant key the store applies (zero violations today; src/lib/ is relaxed because it is the layer that owns the drivers, and src/lib/llm/ is exempt from the chokepoint rule it enforces on everyone else); (3) `no-restricted-exports` refuses `export const dynamic|runtime|revalidate|fetchCache|dynamicParams` under src/app/, the same five rubric A2 blocks in a diff, deliberately excluding maxDuration and preferredRegion, which are Vercel function settings the repo uses. It runs as `npm run lint` inside `npm run check` inside `check:ci` inside the pre-push hook, so a breach fails the build on the machine that wrote it; the fix is the seam, not an eslint-disable. test-unit/lint-fences.test.mjs asserts each fence is still declared at full width, so dropping one restricted name — the cheapest way to make a red build green — turns the unit suite red instead. On the formatter half of the finding: no Prettier or Biome was added, deliberately and now explicitly. ADR-0008 keeps repo tooling on Node built-ins before it takes a dependency, and this session cannot install or run one; the decision is recorded in eslint.config.mjs's header and in AGENTS.md as 'style is not reviewed here, do not reformat files you are not otherwise changing', which is the decision the item asked to be made explicit.

Both named patterns are false at HEAD and are blocked by a required check, so there is nothing to fix and editing prose to satisfy the scanner would be doing the detector rather than the work: sast.yml is triggered by push/pull_request/schedule and contains no pull_request_target (the only occurrences in the repo are the P2 rule's own prose in scripts/actions-pin.mjs and SECURITY.md describing it), and every ${{ }} in agent-review.yml lands in an env: binding with none in a run: body — while scripts/actions-pin.mjs rules P1/P2/P5/P7/P8 run blocking in sast.yml's `workflow-policy` job (a required check) and inside check:ci, so re-introducing either pattern fails the build. A previous Ascent cycle already widened that enforcement to the classes P5 missed (P7: an attacker-controlled context may appear ONLY as an env: binding, never in run:, with: or if:; P8: container images digest-pinned). The one genuinely open supply-chain item in this area is unreachable here: every `uses:` in the repo is first-party, so STRICT=false plus RATCHET.pinned=0 makes actions-pin.mjs green at '0 of N pinned' by exemption. Closing it is `npm run actions:pin` — a networked run that resolves each tag to its commit SHA and writes STRICT=true and the ratchet floor back in the same pass. This session has no network and no shell; inventing 40-hex SHAs would break every workflow rather than pin it. The exact three-step command sequence is already written verbatim in the header of scripts/actions-pin.mjs, which is the file the operator will open.

lessons: This repository answers a maturity gap with a zero-dependency node script wired into `npm run check:ci` (and therefore into .husky/pre-push, which is the real gate because master ships to Vercel on push), plus a test in test-unit/ that fails when the wiring is removed. Before proposing any new practice here, check whether the gap is already covered that way — several scanner findings against this repo are false at HEAD and blocked by its own gates — and when adding one, decide its rung first: blocking only if it passes on the tree today, otherwise reporting with a ratchet (ADR-0007).

When a repo's own ADRs record what a decision could NOT do, that sentence is the highest-value place to work. ADR-0011 said plainly that the required-checks enumeration 'can lie about GitHub's settings, because nothing here can read them without a token' — which was exactly the observability gap a later scan raised. Closing it meant splitting the claim by rung: declare the GitHub side in-repo and gate it offline, then read the live state with a token in a scheduled reporting job and publish the answer where a non-maintainer can read it.

An agent-authored codebase gets more from a lint fence than from another paragraph. eslint-config-next plus nothing means every AGENTS.md 'never' is re-derived from prose on each run; `no-restricted-imports` / `no-restricted-exports` cost no new dependency and turn the chokepoint, the store seam and the segment-config ban into build failures. Draw them narrow enough to verify by exhaustive grep first — in a sandbox with no node_modules you cannot run eslint, so a fence you cannot prove green today is a fence that turns CI red for the next person.
